t: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, during fiscal year 2013, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall, from the National Service Life Insurance Fund under section 1920 of title 38, United States Code, the Veterans’ Special Life Insurance Fund under section 1923 of title 38, United States Code, and the United States Government Life Insurance Fund under section 1955 of title 38, United States Code, reimburse the “General operating expenses, Veterans Benefits Administration” and “Information technology systems” accounts for the cost of administration of the insurance programs financed through those accounts:  Provided, That reimbursement shall be made only from the surplus earnings accumulated in such an insurance program during fiscal year 2013 that are available for dividends in that program after claims have been paid and actuarially determined reserves have been set aside:  Provided further, That if the cost of administration of such an insurance program exceeds the amount of surplus earnings accumulated in that program, reimbursement shall be made only to the extent of such surplus earnings:  Provided further, That the Secretary shall determine the cost of administration for fiscal year 2013 which is properly allocable to the provision of each such insurance program and to the provision of any total disability income insurance included in that insurance program.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision directing the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to reimburse internal VA accounts from insurance fund surplus earnings. The tempting reading is that the Secretary's cost determination is a decision that might involve outside input, but the text provides for no consultation, comment, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. Every actor is inside the federal government, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: the Secretary shall determine the cost of administration for fiscal year 2013 which is properly allocable to the provision of each such insurance program

qwen_block.w: This section mandates internal financial accounting and reimbursement between federal funds and accounts within the Department of Veterans Affairs. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from any party outside the federal government. The actors involved are the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and federal funds, all of which are inside the government.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall... reimburse the “General operating expenses, Veterans Benefits Administration” and “Information technology systems” accounts for the cost of administration of the insurance programs

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision. It tells the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to repay federal administrative accounts out of the surplus earnings of federal life insurance funds. The only decision, how to allocate administrative costs, is made by the Secretary alone, with no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right of review for anyone outside the federal government. Everyone involved is inside the federal government, so this is not participation.
opus.s: the Secretary shall determine the cost of administration for fiscal year 2013 which is properly allocable to the provision of each such insurance program

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates an internal financial reimbursement process within the Department of Veterans Affairs. The Secretary determines costs and reimburses accounts using surplus earnings, but there is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as veterans, states, or the public) before making these determinations. The actors involved are all inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary shall determine the cost of administration for fiscal year 2013 which is properly allocable to the provision of each such insurance program
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary's determination of costs involves some form of consultation or that the insurance programs involve outside parties (veterans). However, the text describes an internal accounting and reimbursement process within the Department of Veterans Affairs. There is no requirement to consult with veterans, states, or other outside entities before making the decision to reimburse accounts. The "participation" definition requires interaction with people *outside* the federal government before a decision is made. Here, the decision is purely administrative and internal.
